newsitem.title: FRANCE: Draft report cuts French wheat, barley export aims.
newsitem.headline: Draft report cuts French wheat, barley export aims.

text.p: French cereals office ONIC on Tuesday prepared a draft report cutting forecasts for wheat and barley exports to countries outside the European Union during the current season, grain industry sources said.

The draft report, which can be fine-tuned before publication next week, projects French soft wheat exports in the year to June 30, 1997, at six million tonnes instead of a previously published forecast of 6.8 million tonnes, they said.
It also establishes a new French barley export goal of 1.2 million tonnes instead of the previous 1.5 million, they said.
The grain authority's regular November report was drafted at a closed-door session of industry experts in Paris on Tuesday.
The industry panel's recommendations are usually accepted by a full body of ONIC members but can be altered before release. The official report is due for publication on November 13.
Industry sources said Tuesday's drafting session had agreed on a higher target for soft wheat exports to France's partners inside the European Union this season.
It recommended a goal of 8.84 million tonnes compared with the 8.3 million published in October, they said.

The panel also drew up a higher export target for barley shipments within the EU, they said. It recommended a new target of 2.1 million tonnes compared with the last official forecast of 1.98 million.
Big crops have lifted projections for non-EU wheat and barley exports from last year's depressed levels, when the EU's central grain authorities were battling to preserve stocks.
France exported 3.75 million tonnes of soft wheat and 221,000 tonnes of barley outside the EU in 1995/96 (July/June).
In the same period it exported 8.6 million tonnes of soft wheat and 2.2 million tonnes of barley inside the EU.

The sources said ONIC was expected to keep its estimate for a record 1996 soft wheat crop broadly unchanged at 34.4 million tonnes, up from last year's 29.8 million. It was expected to shave the 1996 barley crop estimate by a few thousand tonnes to 9.47 million tonnes, up from 7.7 million tonnes the year before.

ONIC was expected to raise its June, 1997, soft wheat carryover estimate to just under 2.3 million tonnes from a previously published 2.127 million and last season's 2.23 million. The barley carryover forecast was seen 200,000 tonnes higher than previously estimated at just under 1.3 million, or around twice last season's closing level of 629,000 tonnes.
